transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Hello Mr. Dubois, it is good to see you again. Please, have a seat.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Thank you. I am glad to be back in this office and not in that holding room.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I wanted to start by talking about what happened during your visit last week. To be very clear, the surgical site was marked incorrectly. The marker was placed on your left arm when the lesion was actually on your right arm.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Yes, and I had to be the one to tell the nurse. I felt... very strange.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I am sorry that this happened. I was the one responsible for marking your skin, and I made a mistake.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: It is not just a mistake. It is a matter of... how can I say... dignité. To be sitting there and realize the doctors do not even know which arm is which. It makes me feel like a piece of meat, not a man.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand. Does that make sense so far, or should I explain the marking process again?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: No, I understand the process. I understand that you were careless. I felt a great sense of alarm. Je me suis senti très inquiet, vraiment.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: The most important thing is that the error was caught before any incision was made.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: But it could have been different. If I had been asleep or if I were more confused, you would have cut the wrong arm.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I know you are upset, but we caught it in time. Now, I just need to make sure we have the follow-up scheduled for the actual excision.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You are not listening to me. I am telling you that my trust is broken. I have always taken pride in being a precise man, and I expect the same from my doctors. To have such a lack of care... it is insulting.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand, but we have to move forward. I have to go to another appointment in a few minutes, so let's wrap this up quickly.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Quickly? You want to finish this quickly? My dignity is not a matter of a quick conversation.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I am just saying that the outcome was safe. We avoided a wrong-site surgery. Do you understand why the mark was misplaced?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I do not care why. I care that it happened.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I apologize for the error, as I said.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: It is a very small apology for a very large failure. C'est inacceptable.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Do you? You seem to be looking at the clock.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I am simply managing my schedule. But the point remains that you are safe.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Safe is the bare minimum. I expected professional excellence.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Right. So, for the plan, we can look at rescheduling the procedure for next month.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: And how do I know you will not mark the wrong arm again?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I will be more careful.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: That is not a plan. That is a wish.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We will likely have a second person verify the mark before you go back into the holding area.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Who is this second person? When will this happen?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Probably the head nurse. I will send a note in your chart about it.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: A note. I see.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: That is the best I can do right now. Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I feel that you are rushing me out of the room.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I really do have another patient waiting.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Of course. My feelings are an inconvenience to your schedule.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I am sorry you feel that way, but we have addressed the facts of the error.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: We have addressed the facts, but you have not addressed the man.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I have apologized for the mistake.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: There is a difference between an apology and an understanding.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I think we have covered everything. I will have my assistant give you the new date for the excision.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I will think about whether I want to return to this clinic.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: That is your choice. I will see you then.

H.justification: Resident uses rushing language repeatedly ('wrap this up quickly', 'managing my schedule', 'another patient waiting') and shows defensive escalation.

E.justification: The error was named explicitly in the first turn using lay language, and comprehension was checked once ('Does that make sense so far?').

A.justification: Resident used direct apology language, took personal responsibility ('I was the one responsible'), and maintained this accountability despite pushback.

R.justification: Resident relied on generic validation ('I understand') and consistently met emotional bids with factual redirection ('the outcome was safe').

T.justification: Resident provided a vague plan to reschedule for 'next month' and a prevention step, but failed to define a named patient role.
